audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagreed with each other. phases and content.win both give Trundle levels 1, 2, 3, 6 and first item with skill windows at 4-5 and 2+ items, but the prose in early, mid and whys[0] through whys[4] hands Galio the whole lane — 'From level 2 onward he owns the exchanges', 'Accept that you are losing lane phase', 'he wins the slow-burn war here'. The packet flags exactly this as 'level chart contradicts data: Trundle wins 52.99% but the chart gives Galio 4/7 stages vs 1'.
audit.why: 52.99% over 234 games plus the kits support the chart, not the prose. Galio's only tool that answers a Frozen Domain trade is Shield of Durand, a charged taunt at 275 range that he walks slowly through — and Trundle's W hands him extra move speed to leave that radius. Justice Punch is an 11s dash that terrain stops, and Pillar of Ice is terrain. Hero's Entrance is 180s and a map ability, not a duel ability.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[0] through whys[4], early and mid so the prose matches the existing chart: Trundle owns 1-3, Levels 4-5 are the Shield of Durand read, and level 6 is Trundle's on Subjugate. No stage was flipped — only the text that contradicted the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Levels 2-3 spike says to 'avoid standing at a wall or minion cluster where the dash extends' and the Levels 4-5 spike treats Shield of Durand as an unanswerable channel taunt. Neither is right — Justice Punch does not extend off walls or minions, and Shield of Durand has a small radius he crawls through.
audit.why: Riot's Justice Punch text: 'Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters' — first CHAMPION, so minions do not stop or extend it, and the derived terrain flag is there because terrain ends the dash. Riot's Shield of Durand text: 'Galio charges a defensive stance, moving slowly. Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies' at 275 range, 18/17/16/15/14.
audit.corrected: Both spikes rebuilt on the real mechanics — Pillar of Ice ends the dash, and Frozen Domain's move speed walks you out of a 275-range charge he can only crawl behind.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] tells the player Galio will 'use his passive Wind Wall'. Galio has no Wind Wall — that is Yasuo's. Galio's passive is Colossal Smash, an empowered auto. Separately, late says Iceborn Gauntlet 'roots Galio inside your Frozen Domain', which is a slow, not a root.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon: Colossal Smash — 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area.' Nothing in Galio's kit blocks projectiles. The decisive real interactions this page was missing are both terrain and radius: Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain and Justice Punch is a dash, and Shield of Durand is only 275 range while Frozen Domain hands you the move speed to leave it.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall removed and replaced with what he actually does with Justice Punch as an escape; 'roots' corrected to 'slows'; the Pillar-stops-the-dash and walk-out-of-the-taunt interactions written into the spikes, the cooldown block and the report.

audit.whatIsWrong: Justice Punch is named as the tracked cooldown on a dozen lines with no duration, and Shield of Durand — the ability that actually decides Levels 4-5 — has none either.
audit.why: Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7, Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14, Winds of War 11/10/9/8/7 at 825 range, Hero's Entrance 180/160/140.
audit.corrected: 11s, 18s and 180s now stated in the cooldown block, the report, the spikes and mid.

edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1 — a dash, and terrain stops it, so Pillar the line. - Shield of Durand: 18s, 275 range.

edits.before: At level 1 it is a genuine coin flip — your Chomp bites for real damage and steals his AD, but Galio's passive stacks a magic-damage shield empowered auto that pokes back for free. Open Q and bite him on every last-hit attempt to establish the steal before he reaches level 2. The critical rule for this entire early lane: never stand inside Justice Punch range when it is up. Galio's E knocks you up and interrupts your Frozen Domain plant mid-animation — if you place W and he dashes through you before it activates, you lose the trade entirely. From level 2 onward he owns the exchanges: he can E-into-Q-into-taunt-W your pattern and walk away through the MR he is stacking. Accept that you are losing lane phase, last-hit cleanly under tower if needed, and do not give him a kill that lets him snowball his roam.
edits.after: At level 1 you are the aggressor — Chomp bites for real damage and saps his AD, while Colossal Smash gives Galio only one empowered auto in reply. Open Q and bite him on every last-hit attempt to bank the steal before he reaches level 2. The rule that matters most early: Justice Punch is a dash on an 11-second cooldown and it stops dead on terrain, so once Pillar of Ice is up at level 3 his only way into you is gone — drop it across his line rather than behind him. Before that, respect the knockup, because it hits the first champion it reaches and it will interrupt a Frozen Domain plant mid-animation: place W first and step in second, never the other way round. Levels 1 through 3 are yours. Take the trades, bank the wave, and do not hand him a kill that funds a roam.

edits.before: The midgame is still Galio's window through level 6 on paper, but your level 6 Subjugate changes the math permanently. The moment he shows Justice Punch is down — usually after a failed roam or a wasted trade — drop Frozen Domain, run him down inside it, and cast Subjugate the second he activates W to taunt. You drain his MR onto yourself while he is mid-channel, and the resist-stack means his follow-up Q and passive auto hit a much tankier Trundle than the one he was trading with at level 3. Force this pattern every time his cooldowns are down. If he has not committed his dash, do not all-in — wait him out inside the domain until he burns it, then cash in.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the read. Shield of Durand is an 18-second charged taunt at only 275 range and Galio crawls while charging it, so Frozen Domain's move speed is enough to leave the radius and make it release on nothing — but if he catches you in it you lose that trade outright. Level 6 settles the lane. Hero's Entrance is 180 seconds and a map tool rather than a duel tool, so the 1v1 belongs to Subjugate: the moment he commits the taunt or burns Justice Punch, cast R, drain his magic resist onto yourself, and finish on your own ice. If he has committed neither, wait him out inside the domain instead of walking into the charge.

edits.before: Two items is where this matchup fully resolves in your favor. Iceborn Gauntlet turns every Chomp into a point-blank AOE slow that roots Galio inside your Frozen Domain against his will; Trinity Force Spellblade procs scale your Chomp into genuine burst damage. In teamfights, Subjugate on Galio (or any front-line tank he is paired with) turns his team's own defensive stats into your armor and MR stack — you become nearly unkillable while they lose their resistance base. Track Galio's ultimate globally: his R Hero's Entrance lets him cancel your dives on other lanes, so coordinate objectives and dives while his R is on cooldown. In the side lane 1v1 with two items and Subjugate up, Galio has no realistic answer to you.

edits.before: Galio's passive empowers his first auto with bonus magic damage — a free poke that doesn't cost him mana or a spell. Neither of you commits here; last-hit and feel out the range.
edits.after: Chomp is one of the hardest-hitting level-1 spells in the game and it saps his AD; Colossal Smash answers with a single empowered auto, which does not cover a full melee exchange.

edits.before: Justice Punch (E) is fully online and his level-2 combo extends the dash off minions or walls — he controls the all-in threat and you cannot safely drop Frozen Domain without it being interrupted.
edits.after: Frozen Domain lands before Justice Punch can matter: on your own ice the move speed and attack speed let you take a short trade and leave before his 825-range Winds of War ticks for anything real.

edits.before: With Q-W-E live Galio can chain Justice Punch into his full taunt-W rotation — he interrupts your Frozen Domain and walks out of the zone healthier than you.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice completes the kit and Justice Punch is a dash that terrain stops — with the pillar across his line, his only engage into you is simply unavailable.

edits.before: Shield of Durand (W) taunt pulls you off Frozen Domain mid-pattern and his stacked MR means your physical bite damage barely trades through it — he wins the slow-burn war here.
edits.after: Shield of Durand is the one tool that genuinely answers you: an 18s charged taunt that drags you off the ice. It is 275 range and he crawls while charging, so this window is a pure read.

edits.before: Galio's level 6 ultimate Hero's Entrance gives him a global safety net: he can recall, roam, and return faster than you can punish. He dictates the map tempo while you are stuck earning back the lane deficit.
edits.after: Subjugate beats Hero's Entrance in a 1v1 — his R is 180 seconds and a map tool, not a duel tool. Cast yours the moment he commits Shield of Durand and fight the rest of it on his own magic resist.

edits.before: Two items and Subjugate on cooldown reset: Iceborn Gauntlet slow locks Galio inside Frozen Domain, the resistance drain strips whatever tankiness he has built, and your Chomp AD steal makes his MR stack irrelevant — the 1v1 is Trundle's.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet's slow holds Galio inside Frozen Domain and the resistance drain strips what he built, so the side lane is yours — but his shields, the taunt and a global Hero's Entrance still make the five-versus-five his. Split, do not group into him.

notes: Two layers were contradicting each other. phases and content.win both give Trundle five of seven stages, but early, mid and whys[0]-whys[4] narrated Galio winning the lane ('Accept that you are losing lane phase'). That is the packet's flagged defect. I aligned the prose to the existing chart rather than flipping any stage, because the chart also matches the 52.99% over 234 games and the kit reading. Killed a fabricated ability: wants.foe[2] told the player Galio would 'use his passive Wind Wall' — Galio has no Wind Wall, that is Yasuo; his passive is Colossal Smash. Also corrected 'Land Justice Punch into a wall or minion cluster to extend the knockup' (Riot's text says it knocks up the first CHAMPION it encounters, and terrain ends the dash rather than extending it) and 'Iceborn Gauntlet roots Galio' (it slows). The two decisive interactions now on the page are Pillar of Ice ending an 11s dash, and Frozen Domain's move speed walking you out of a 275-range charge Galio can only crawl behind.
